advisory.summary: The SPEC-2 fix replaced a closed parenthetical with an unpaired em-dash appositive, leaving the three-item plan-override list ambiguous: the `Overridden:` clause can be read as continuing the test-runner appositive instead of the third list item.
advisory.evidence: Fix commit 7b0a931 changed the plan clause from "`Test runner: <runner> - <why>` only when the repository has none (so the user can object at the approver gate), and `Overridden: ENG-n - <repo rule that wins>`" to "only when the repository has none — the language's conventional default, named with the reason so the user can object at the approver gate, and `Overridden: ENG-n - <repo rule that wins>`". The em-dash opens an appositive with no closing delimiter, so the comma before ", and `Overridden: ...`" closes either the second outer list item or the appositive. tasks.md T006 words the same clause with parentheses — "(the language's conventional default, so the user can object at the approver gate)" — so the fix drifted from its own spec's punctuation; constitution Writing Standards require instructions to be unambiguous. Same wording is rendered into all eight dist copies, in sync with core.
advisory.fix: Restore a closed delimiter in core/roles/spec-builder.md line 31: "`Test runner: <runner> - <why>` only when the repository has none (the language's conventional default, named with the reason so the user can object at the approver gate), and `Overridden: ENG-n - <repo rule that wins>` per override or `Overridden: none`", then re-render all four harnesses and commit dist/ with the source (constitution III).
